newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Senate rejects privatization bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Senate rejects privatization bill.

text.p: Brazil's Senate rejected a bill which would have allowed for the removal of state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) and other companies from the government's privatization program, an official said.
The upper house voted 28-24 to take that action, the official said.

The bill's author, Sen. Jose Eduardo Dutra of the left-wing Workers Party (PT), said he would seek to put forward next year another bill giving Congress powers to remove companies from the privatization program.
Dutra is a leading critic of the CVRD selloff due to begin in March 1997.

Many senators are reported to be unhappy with the plan for the company's privatization, principally because the government has not agreed to their demands that cash be used for regional infrastructure projects.
Senior government officials, like Finance Minister Pedro Malan, insist the receipts, expected to total about $6.0 billion, be used for debt retirement.
